Responsibilities

About Us

Parker Meggitt occupies a leading position in the design and manufacture of aircraft engine shell-and-tube and plate-and-fin heat exchangers. We are a significant supplier to both civil and military aviation, with products used on the majority of the latest aeroengines, including LEAP, PurePower and F135.

Position Overview

Responsible for the design, development, and qualification of Thermal Management Systems products for aerospace applications, supporting programmes from initial concept through production implementation. The role has a strong focus on the design of aerospace heat exchangers and associated mechanical components, requiring application of sound mechanical engineering principles and aerospace design practices to deliver innovative, reliable, and complaint solutions that meet customer specifications and airworthiness requirements.

Working in the Design Engineering team, this role will work collaboratively with cross-functional teams and external stakeholders leading new product development and continuous improvement initiatives. The role involves translating requirements into robust design solutions, ensuring performance, quality, and manufacturability objectives are achieved.

Key Responsibilities

  • Lead the design and development of aerospace thermal managements products, including heat exchangers and mechanical components, from concept through full product lifecycle, including production implementation.
  • Interpret customer specifications and airworthiness requirements to define design parameters, ensuring compliance with performance, safety, and regulatory standards.
  • Develop detailed product specifications by analysing functional requirements, materials, performance, cost, manufacturability, and operational efficiency.
  • Create and maintain design data including engineering drawings, 3D CAD models, and bill of materials in accordance with established engineering standards.
  • Validate and verify design performance through analysis, testing, and interpretation of results, ensuring conformance to qualification requirements and reliability targets.
  • Evaluate and disposition non-conforming product in accordance with quality and engineering standards, defining and implementing appropriate corrective actions.

Essential skills and experience you’ll need to be considered for this position

  • Bachelor’s degree in mechanical engineering or a related technical discipline
  • 3-5 years of relevant engineering experience, preferably in aerospace or related (regulated) industries
  • Strong experience in the use of commercial CAD software systems
  • Solid understanding of engineering principles, product design, and industry standards, with the ability to apply knowledge across technical disciplines
  • Knowledge of GD&T principles for component design and assembly
  • Knowledge of manufacturing processes including, but not limited to, forging, casting, CNC machining, welding, brazing and sheet metal forming
  • Strong analytical, problem-solving and continuous improvement mindset with experience applying engineering best practices and process improvements
  • Effective communication skills, with the ability to present technical information and collaborate with cross-functions teams, customers, and suppliers

What We Offer

Parker Meggitt is proud to offer a competitive total rewards framework designed with our colleagues' health, wealth, and well-being in mind to help our employees balance a successful career. Our competitive package will include:

  • Funded membership of a professional body
  • Focused career development planning with opportunities to progress
  • Pension scheme with up to 10% matching company contribution
  • Income protection scheme
  • Life Assurance x4 basic salary
  • Share buying scheme
  • 25 days holiday, plus bank holidays, with the option to buy and sell up to 5 days
  • Service-related holiday (3 years = 1 day and increase up to max 5 days)
  • Cash Plan or Private Medical Cover
  • Employee Assistance Program for Health & Wellbeing
  • Free on-site car parking
  • Employee Referral Scheme
  • An on-site restaurant and Starbucks offering subsidised food
  • Employee Perks – offering our employees discounts on a huge variety of goods and services

Parker Hannifin EMEA Sàrl (“PHEMEA”), based in Etoy, Switzerland, is the Principal Operating Company for Parker in the EMEA region. It is supported by a network of Parker Manufacturing Divisions and Sales Company Entities. The Aerospace Group EMEA is a strategic business Group within PHEMEA. Hydraulic Systems Division EMEA (HSDE) is a key service provider to PHEMEA.

Our Leicester based client can demonstrate almost half a centurys expertise in the design, development and manufacture of bespoke automation and robotic systems for a diverse range of industry sectors and are regarded by many in the industry as one of the leading automation system solution providers in the whole of the UK.

As a result of continued success and a planned programme of strategic growth, they are now seeking to recruit an experienced Lead / Senior Mechanical Design Engineer to complement their established and successful team and deliver innovative special purpose automation machinery projects.

Tasked with both designing and overseeing an array of special purpose machine projects from order acceptance to customer hand over, the successful Senior Mechanical Design Engineer candidate will be responsible for the design, detailing and successful delivery of multiple projects, communicating effectively with customers, suppliers and team members as required and working as part of a team dedicated to delivering projects to on time and within budget.

After attending sales hand over meetings and committing to an overall project plan and budget, you will perform mechanical design and detailing functions for multiple projects allocated to you using 3D CAD within the time allocated in the project plan, and will arrange Design Reviews during the design process to ensure they are well executed, meet overall requirements, are designed for assembly, robust and reliable operation, and meet or better budgetary constraints whilst minimising any development issues that may arise.

You will also obtain a Design Pass Off by the customer on time and to project plan and ensure that BOMs are produced on time and within budget, and will negotiate with external suppliers in order to obtain the most cost:efficient materials in line with project budgets and timing plans. You will also be responsible for assisting the electrical design process by communicating clearly and effectively through the duration of the project and especially through the mechanical design phase, and will compile a build folder and communicate build details to the machine tool fitters to ensure an efficient build process.

Other responsibilities for the Senior Mechanical Design Engineer role will include providing direction and support to fitters, electricians and other engineers within the team as required, and undertaking visits to customer sites as appropriate to fully understand the customer requirements and to obtain measurements for all dimensions, drawings, site layouts and other considerations, and will document and communicate all such requirements to the customer and internal staff respectively.

You will assess and improve design concepts along with a team at sales quotation stage to reduce risks, costs, lead times and be skilled in identifying key risks and assist in compiling plans for trials to reduce them.

You will obtain all parts, samples and drawings necessary in advance to ensure these can be checked and used through the design phase and will check the design work produced by other designers to ensure accuracy of design work, as well as conducting project reviews with customers on a periodic basis and reporting on the status of each project whilst constructing and maintaining a comprehensive Technical Construction File (TCF) which includes manuals, risk assessments, mechanical parts list and drawings.

Other duties will include carrying out machine risk assessments during the design phase to ensure Machinery Directive requirements are met and leading projects during the development and installation phases of the project with pro:active and timely delivery of problem fixes whilst ensuring that all H and S and safety rules, guidelines and policies are understood and adhered to at all times.

We are seeking a senior mechanical engineer for one of our offices in the north- Manchester, Leeds, Newcastle, Glasgow or Whitehaven- with experience delivering water utility projects.   • Good knowledge of pumping system design standards and best practice.

Job Description

Job Overview:

The HVAC Mechanical Engineer applies their conceptual knowledge of mechanicals and with a moderate level of guidance and direction from colleagues and leadership, is responsible for solving a range of straightforward HVAC problems. They will be responsible for analyzing possible solutions using standard procedures, as well as building knowledge of the company, processes, and customers. The HVAC Mechanical Engineer understands key business drivers and applies this knowledge to solve problems in straightforward situations through analysis of possible solutions using technical experience, judgment, and precedents.

Responsibilities

Key Tasks and Responsibilities:

  • Perform FEED, Studies, and detailed design engineering, analysis, and calculations on more complex and demanding engineering tasks
  • Apply knowledge and skills to complete varied assignments
  • Prepare clear and accurate detailed design calculations and analyses including design reports and procedures
  • Prioritize and organize own work to meet deadlines
  • Focus on completing work within budgets
  • Communicate and explain information clearly in straightforward engineering activities
  • Apply all relevant procedures, practices, and international standards according to their discipline (Static, Rotating, Package, and special equipment), and applicable as per the Project requirements
  • Ensure all relevant McDermott procedures, practices, and quality standards are implemented
  • Perform mechanical calculations related to the respective discipline (pressure vessels preliminary calculations, rotating equipment pre-dimensioning, power consumption determination, etc.)
  • Perform Mechanical data sheets and equipment specifications by process and project requirements
  • Manage equipment requisitions by project requirements
  • Evaluate technical quotations, prepare queries, compile technical bid tabulations and recommendations, prepare purchase requisitions, and coordinate with Procurement to expedite vendor documentation
  • Perform the drawings, documents, and inspection & test procedures review from the sellers and manufacturers
  • Coordinate with other engineering disciplines the interdisciplinary review of supplier documentation
  • Assist inspections during testing and evaluate test results of equipment, both if necessary
  • Perform Final inspections at the Manufacturer’s workshop when required by the project
  • Provide technical inputs to subcontracts related to Mechanical engineering (Equipment erection, Equipment insulation installation, etc.)
  • Ensure good coordination with all other concerned disciplines
  • Execute project closeout activities and communicate lessons learned
  • Assist the Mechanical lead with the Control changes and report deviations to the project management team
  • Apply all the relevant HSE requirements and criteria in the engineering work and decisions

Reports to: Project: Lead Engineer Functional: Supervising/Lead Engineer or Engineering Manager

Liaise with: All design/drafting disciplines, all Engineering disciplines, fabrication groups, and Document Control

Supervises: Associate /Trainee Mechanical Engineers

  • Bachelor’s degree in Engineering (Master’s Degree is Preferred)
  • 3-8 years of experience in oil and gas with major contractors or consultants predominantly performing detail design
  • Preferably Registered Engineer in Training (ElT) or member of a professional engineering society
  • Good English in writing/speaking (B2 Level Quality-oriented and schedule-conscious
  • Leadership skills and willingness to coordinate some discipline tasks
  • Make recommendations to improve the work process
  • Give support to construction, when necessary, from the office or at the site

What You Will Do

  • Lead the research, design, development, modification, evaluation, and improvement of mechanical and electro-mechanical modules, assemblies, and subsystems.

  • Experience working within regulated medical device product development environments.

  • Experience using Computer-Aided Engineering (CAE) tools to support product design and development.
  • Understanding of clinical procedures and their application to product development activities.

Plymouth or Exeter.

About the role

We have a brand-new opportunity for an Associate Mechanical Engineer to join our team based in our Plymouth or Exeter offices.

companyName: Guy's and St Thomas' NHS Foundation Trust
jobDescription:
Essentia, part of Guy’s and St Thomas’ NHS Foundation Trust, is seeking a Senior Mechanical Engineer to provide professional leadership and technical authority for mechanical infrastructure across the Trust’s estate. The role will safeguard patient and staff wellbeing by overseeing technical standards, statutory compliance, risk management and resilience across critical mechanical assets and systems.


Guy’s and St Thomas’ NHS Foundation Trust is one of the country’s largest and busiest NHS trusts, comprising Guy’s, St Thomas’, Evelina London Children’s Hospital, Royal Brompton and Harefield, alongside community services in Lambeth and Southwark. Its clinical services are supported by a complex, operationally critical estate where safety, resilience and the patient experience are paramount.


Essentia is the Trust’s operational and infrastructure delivery group. Working across the Trust’s hospital, community and partner sites, it brings together engineering, estates, capital development, facilities management, digital technology and other essential services to maintain safe, resilient and high-performing healthcare environments.


The successful candidate will demonstrate substantial expertise in the management, maintenance and development of complex mechanical infrastructure within large, operationally critical environments. This should include experience across heating, ventilation and air conditioning systems, medical gas pipeline systems, steam and pressure systems, and water systems. They will lead estate assurance and compliance, support asset lifecycle planning and infrastructure investment, and drive continuous improvement in safety, resilience, performance and value for money.


Candidates should hold relevant professional qualifications and training, ideally including a mechanical engineering degree and professional membership of IMechE or CIBSE, or Chartered Engineer status, alongside Authorised Person duties and safe systems of work experience in areas such as medical gas pipeline systems, critical ventilation and pressure systems. Strong knowledge of healthcare engineering standards, including Health Technical Memoranda, will be important. The appointed individual will be a confident, methodical and resilient leader who can explain technical risk clearly, engage and influence stakeholders, and demonstrate Essentia’s caring, ambitious and inclusive values.


To learn more about the role, view the Candidate Brochure at: Essentia -Senior Mechanical Engineer


To arrange a confidential briefing discussion, please contact our retained search adviser Connor Humpage connor.humpage@mrgglobal.com at MRG.


Applications should consist of a CV and supporting statement and can be sent to connor.humpage@mrgglobal.com


The closing date for applications is Sunday 25th October 2026.

The Role

SES Engineering Services are looking for a Senior Mechanical Engineer to join our Northwest team to support on technically complex Mechanical and Electrical projects across the Northwest region.

If you are an established Leader looking for an opportunity to challenge the norm, bring fresh new ideas and elevate yourself within the industry then join us and help to create tomorrow together.

This is a great opportunity to progress your career as part of a talented, diverse, and supportive team.

What You'll Be Doing

Our Senior Mechanical Engineers are a valuable part of our business, the focus of this role will be to provide visible leadership, insight, direction and foresight in the safe and profitable delivery of schemes, while also providing excellent customer satisfaction and successfully developing a team.

  • Lead, mentor, and develop mechanical engineers and project teams, fostering a culture of collaboration, continuous improvement, and engineering excellence.

Graduate Mechanical Building Services Engineer

Tetra Tech 2027 Graduate Scheme: Your Launchpad to a Consultancy Career

Join our two-year Graduate Scheme and kickstart your career with hands-on experience, expert mentorship, and a tailored development plan. You’ll work on a variety of real-world projects, develop both technical and professional skills, and be encouraged to share your ideas and shape your future.

The Role

We’re seeking talented graduates to join our Building Services team in Birmingham or Manchester. You’ll work alongside experienced engineers and contribute to the design and delivery of building systems that support healthier, more sustainable environments. From education and healthcare to commercial and residential developments, you'll help shape spaces that are comfortable, efficient and future-ready.

Your Impact In This Position

As a Graduate Mechanical Building Services Engineer, you’ll play a key role in supporting the technical delivery of projects. You’ll gain hands-on experience delivering innovative solutions that integrate mechanical and electrical systems. We’re passionate about reducing environmental impact and meeting the evolving demands of modern buildings through smart, sustainable design.

You’ll collaborate across disciplines, attend client meetings and site visits, and produce technical drawings and calculations that meet industry standards. With mentorship from senior engineers and access to a structured development programme, you’ll build the skills, confidence, and experience needed to progress toward chartership and beyond.

What To Expect

  • Mentorship & Support: Learn from experienced professionals and receive guidance from a dedicated technical mentor in your chosen discipline.
  • Structured Learning: Benefit from a blend of formal training, project-based learning, and self-directed study.
  • Personal Development: Build your consultancy skills through a mix of technical and interpersonal training, with regular feedback and reviews
  • Community: Start with a central induction alongside your graduate peers and become part of a collaborative, supportive network.

Programme Highlights

  • Central induction and ongoing support from your line manager and mentor
  • In-depth technical training in your core discipline, plus exposure to 15 technical and 8 interpersonal topics
  • Quarterly development reviews to track your progress
  • Opportunities to shadow senior colleagues and contribute to diverse projects

Your Pathway: You’ll be assigned a location, cost centre, line manager, and a ‘home’ technical discipline based on your qualifications and business needs. If you wish to explore a different discipline at the end of the programme, we’ll consider this based on your interests and business requirements.

Chartered Management Institute (CMI) Partnership

As part of the scheme, you’ll have access to the CMI Foundation Chartered Manager pathway through flexible, online Bite Size programs. Choose from a range of topics—including Managing Change, Leading in a Digital Age, Conflict Resolution, Project Management, and Data-Driven Decision Making—to build your leadership and management skills.

CMI Bite Size Benefits

  • Short, focused modules you can complete at your own pace
  • Practical insights to strengthen your management capabilities
  • Internationally recognised certification upon completion
  • Option to progress to a Level 5 Award in Leadership and Management

Each program consists of three concise modules (totalling 85-135 minutes), scheduled in your second year. Complete activity sheets to demonstrate your learning and earn your Foundation Chartered Manager certification.

Qualifications

Must have achieved, or be on track to achieve, a relevant degree in either Mechanical Engineering or Building Services Engineering.

Working Environment

This is a hybrid role with three to four days per week in the Birmingham or Manchester office. You’ll enjoy a collaborative environment that values technical excellence and work-life balance. We place a strong emphasis on employee wellbeing

Application and Selection Process

To apply for the Tetra Tech 2027 Graduate Scheme, candidates must submit an up-to-date CV detailing their academic background, relevant experience, and motivation for joining the programme. All applications will be acknowledged upon receipt.

Following initial screening, shortlisted candidates will be invited to complete online psychometric testing designed to evaluate key competencies and problem-solving skills relevant to consultancy work. Those who progress beyond this stage will be invited to attend an in-person Graduate Day.

The closing date for applications in this round is 31st October 2026. We encourage early submissions to ensure full consideration.

Ready to build your expertise and shape your future? Apply now and start your journey with Tetra Tech.

Tetra Tech is a leading provider of consulting and engineering services working across the full project lifecycle worldwide. We have a wide range of expertise across our teams, providing a global support network with a personalised approach to client relationships to better understand where we can add value. We support public and private sector clients on local, national, and international projects to deliver sustainable and resilient solutions. Product Design Engineer

Location: Goole

Salary: £28,000–£30,000


We are currently recruiting for a Product Design Engineer to join a manufacturing business based in Goole.


The role will involve supporting the design and development of products from concept through to manufacture, working closely with engineering and production teams to ensure designs are practical and meet customer requirements.


Key responsibilities:

  • Creating and modifying 3D CAD models and technical drawings
  • Supporting new product development and design improvements
  • Producing accurate manufacturing drawings and documentation
  • Working with production and engineering teams to resolve design issues
  • Supporting the introduction of new products into manufacture
  • Ensuring designs meet required specifications and standards


The ideal candidate will have:

  • Experience in a product design or mechanical design environment
  • Good knowledge of 3D CAD
  • Ability to interpret and produce technical drawings
  • An engineering/manufacturing background
  • Strong attention to detail and problem-solving skills

Job Description

Your impact

You’ll work at the heart of multidisciplinary project teams, advising on thermal performance and ensuring our products meet demanding environmental and operational requirements. This role is ideal for someone with a strong analytical mindset, a flair for problem-solving, and the ability to manage complex interdependencies across multiple programmes and business units.

Leonardo is seeking an experienced Thermal Engineer to play a key role in the development and production of leading-edge Defence products within Land, Naval, Seeker and Space domains supporting both new innovations and proven legacy products.

The successful candidate will be responsible for conducting Thermal Analysis, communicating the results and advising on all aspects of Thermal Engineering activities. The role will involve working with multi-discipline project teams and our Customers across the UK.

What You’ll Do

  • Conduct thermal analysis of mechanical designs to assess performance and safety using thermal analysis software, CFD techniques, and classical hand calculations.
  • Provide expert guidance on cooling strategies and recommend thermal design improvements as required.
  • Advise on materials and manufacturing techniques with an emphasis on thermal performance and mechanical integrity.
  • Define thermal requirements and develop methods for verifying compliance across Leonardo products.
  • Drive innovation in thermal design, introducing new technologies and methodologies.
  • Support product development through all phases—from design and testing to final certification.
  • Deliver thermal solutions that meet performance requirements on time and within budget.
  • Contribute to technical documentation, including material for peer reviews and stage/gate approvals.
  • All members of the Analysis Team are encouraged and supported to continually develop their skills, including (but not limited to) Structural, Thermal, Pressure and Model Driven domains.
  • This role is located at our team facility but may require occasional travel to our other UK sites.

What You’ll Bring

  • Degree in Mechanical or Aeronautical Engineering
  • Post-graduate experience in Thermal engineering. Proven expertise in thermal analysis, with a track record of developing equipment for challenging and extreme operating environments.
  • Proficiency in CFD tools, preferably Ansys Icepak and Ansys Fluent, alongside a solid foundation in classical hand calculation methods.
  • Experience of environmental test methods for design verification and working knowledge of design certification for land based and airborne equipment.
  • Knowledge of Regulatory Standards including but not limited to: Def Stan 00-970, Health and Safety HSE Regulations including Hazardous Waste Regulation. Compliance with Pressure Equipment Regulation, Pressure System Safety Regulation and Fluorinated Gas Regulations.
  • Awareness of equipment safety compliance requirements, including the ability to support inspection processes and generate fault and failure reports.
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills with the ability to influence the direction of both internal and external customers.
  • A proven problem solver with a practical, pragmatic approach.
  • Ability to take ownership of work packages, planning and scheduling own workload and the work of others.

Desirable

  • It is advantageous for the candidate to have experience in the design, development and test of electronics packaging and/or aerospace equipment.
  • Experience of manufacturing and joining techniques, engineering material properties.
  • Professional recognition as a Chartered Engineer and full membership of a relevant engineering institution (e.g. IMechE)

This is not an exhaustive list, and we are keen to hear from you even if you might not have experience in all the above. The most important skill is a good attitude and willingness to learn.

Working Pattern: Onsite regularly, up to 5 days a week (37 hours standard work week, overtime if approved by project and employee) to delivery security classification and role specific tasks for projects. The company allows hybrid working so working from home is possible when project work allows.

Basildon is the primary location option but Southampton or Bristol is possible.

Security Clearance

Requirements

This role is subject to pre-employment screening in line with the UK Government’s Baseline Personnel Security Standard (BPSS). An additional range of Personnel Security Controls referred to as National Security Vetting (NSV) and ITAR may apply, this could include meeting the eligibility requirements for The Security Check (SC) or Developed Vetting (DV). Job Description

Join Ramboll’s UK Healthcare team as an Associate Mechanical Engineer and lead mechanical engineering design for technically challenging hospital and healthcare projects in the UK and internationally. You’ll shape resilient, low‑carbon building services solutions, deliver coordinated BIM workflows and act as a confident client‑facing technical lead across multi‑disciplinary teams.

If you’re passionate about innovative engineering that improves patient care and drives sustainable change, this role offers the scope and variety to make a real impact.

This advertisement is specifically for Maverick United Consulting Engineers ("Maverick"), an engineering consultancy based in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia. 

Maverick United Consulting Engineers ('Maverick') is an engineering consultancy providing specialist structural, infrastructural and value engineering consultancy services for the built environment.

  • Prepare design deliverables including basis of design reports, schematics, layouts, equipment schedules, specifications, and tender documentation.
  • Review contractor submittals, shop drawings, and technical queries, and provide technical support during construction and installation works.
  • Support testing, commissioning, equipment start-up, functional testing, and handover activities, including reviewing as-built drawings and O&M manuals.

  • Bachelor's Degree in Mechanical Engineering or a related field.
  • Minimum 5 to 8 years of Mechanical Engineering design experience, preferably within an engineering consultancy environment.
  • Strong knowledge of HVAC, ventilation, chilled water, pumping, piping, and associated mechanical systems.

 The Mechanical and Thermal Engineering Team, based in Great Baddow, Chelmsford, is seeking a Mechanical Engineer to join an interdisciplinary team within BAE Systems Digital Intelligence. The position requires a flair for innovation and design as well as proven analytical and problem solving skills.

The Group is involved in the development of future aerospace, security and defence systems.  Areas of application include: structural design of electrical, optical and electro-magnetic devices and mechanisms; analysis of systems subject to harsh operating environments; and the development of thermal management solutions.

 

Tasks Include:

  1. Receiving, interpreting and clarifying instructions from customers or colleagues and providing feedback and design input to help develop the design concept.
  2. Designing and detailing design solutions based on information received and one’s own work.  Designs will be developed using CAD systems by producing 3D solid models of the parts and assemblies involved, supported by calculations and analysis where appropriate, then producing mechanical drawings and other data to facilitate manufacture and assembly.
  3. Designs may need to be analysed to ensure the structural integrity and thermal management performance.
  4. Production of design descriptions and performance reports for design review and communications with the customer.
  5. Provide design for manufacture advice, offer knowledge of new materials and manufacturing techniques.
  6. To provide the design and manufacture details for of 1st off prototypes through to approved production ready design data packs.
  7. Peer review of colleagues designs

 

As a Mechanical Engineer your main responsibilities will involve:

  • To provide a mechanical engineering design service and to promote and demonstrate best practice when using the BAE SYSTEMS preferred toolsets.
  • Innovating to develop new technology and techniques associated with mechanical design and thermal management.
  • Whenever practicable introduce new materials and processes which could realise reduced production costs in support of BAE Systems’ future products
  • Liaising with customers (internal and external) to understand and develop requirements and then provide bespoke solutions supported by appropriate analysis.
  • Reporting findings clearly and concisely, both written and verbal.

 

As a Mechanical Engineer your skills and qualifications will ideally include:

  • A good degree in mechanical engineering or other engineering sciences and equivalent qualifications and as well as appropriate experience.
  • An excellent technical background, with a sound knowledge of mechanical design, structural analysis, design for manufacture and materials.
  • Ability to use Computer Aided Design (CAD) and Finite Element (FE) tools and Microsoft Office.
  • Ability to work with a high level of self-direction, together with occasional supervision and development of other engineers.
  • Knowledge of basic environmental testing methods.
  • Heat transfer and thermal management experience would be beneficial
  • Good interpersonal skills are required as much of the work is team based.
  • An ability and willingness to learn new skills and techniques.
  • Preparation of technical reports, test procedures, process specifications and other product documentation is desirable.

 

What we’re looking for in you:

The successful candidate will work cooperatively and collaboratively with others, be part of a team and will have the ability to identify a problem, obstacle or opportunity and take action in light of this to address current or future problems or opportunities.  You will have excellent communication skills with strong attention to detail and will be flexible, team-focused and deliverables driven.

This role requires SC security clearance and you may also need DV clearance in the future to be able to work across the full spectrum of areas the Group is involved with.

Life at BAE Systems Digital Intelligence 

We are embracing Hybrid Working. This means you and your colleagues may be working in different locations, such as from home, another BAE Systems office or client site, some or all of the time, and work might be going on at different times of the day.

By embracing technology, we can interact, collaborate and create together, even when we’re working remotely from one another. Hybrid Working allows for increased flexibility in when and where we work, helping us to balance our work and personal life more effectively, and enhance well-being.

Diversity and inclusion are integral to the success of BAE Systems Digital Intelligence. We are proud to have an organisational culture where employees with varying perspectives, skills, life experiences and backgrounds – the best and brightest minds – can work together to achieve excellence and realise individual and organisational potential.

jobTitle: Lead Mechanical Engineer – Rotating Electrical Machines
jobDescription:
Job Description Summary

This is an opportunity to work as part of cross-functional team to deliver product designs that meet customer and project requirements in close conjunction with Electrical and Mechanical Engineers and collaborate with Customers and Project Management, Sourcing and Procurement, Manufacturing and Quality teams.

Job Description

At GE Vernova's Rugby site, we engineer some of the most technically demanding rotating electrical machines in the industry — equipment that underpins critical energy infrastructure around the world. As a Lead Mechanical Engineer, you'll take a leading role in the structural and mechanical design of large electrical machines, applying advanced finite element analysis (FEA) and prototype testing expertise to ensure our machines perform reliably across the most demanding operating environments.

This is a role for an experienced mechanical engineer who understands the unique challenges of rotating machine design — someone who combines rigorous analytical capability with practical engineering judgement and the confidence to collaborate across customer, manufacturing, and project teams to deliver real-world solutions.

What You'll Do

You'll lead and contribute across the full mechanical design lifecycle — from requirements capture through to prototype testing and design documentation. Specifically, you will:

  • Lead mechanical machine design — specify, design, and engineer the mechanical aspects of large rotating electrical machines; interpret and resolve contractual and technical requirements in a timely, quality-focused manner; and create and submit design documentation to communicate and record design progress.
  • Drive structural analysis and simulation — lead detailed analytical and finite element analysis (FEA) programmes using ANSYS/Workbench to assess mechanical stress, fatigue, and structural integrity across a range of machine designs and operating conditions.
  • Improve machine performance and competitiveness — lead design model and prototype test programmes to characterise and improve noise and vibration behaviour; investigate new materials and manufacturing methods to enhance machine competitiveness and long-term reliability.
  • Collaborate with customers and cross-functional teams — work closely with customers, third parties, electrical engineers, project management, sourcing, procurement, manufacturing, and quality teams to understand requirements and deliver effective mechanical design solutions.
  • Contribute to engineering excellence — apply and develop knowledge of relevant industry standards and engineering design processes; identify opportunities to advance mechanical engineering tools, methods, and practices across the team.

Who We're Looking For

You're an experienced mechanical engineer with a strong background in structural analysis and rotating machine design, proven FEA capability, and the confidence to lead technical programmes and work effectively with customers and cross-functional partners.

Required

  • A degree in Mechanical Engineering or a closely related discipline. A formal qualification is relevant to the depth of analytical and design work required in this role; however, we are equally interested in your total experience and professional achievements — significant, proven experience in a rotating electrical machines engineering environment will be considered.
  • Significant experience in mechanical engineering for rotating electrical machines, including structural design, analysis, and development.
  • Proven expertise in 2D and/or 3D finite element analysis (FEA) for mechanical designs, including stress and fatigue analysis, using tools such as ANSYS/Workbench.
  • Strong working knowledge of rotating electrical machines — their mechanical engineering challenges, structural characteristics, and manufacturing processes.
  • Familiarity with relevant industry standards including International Organisation for Standardisation (ISO) 9000, BS EN, and International Electrotechnical Commission (IEC) 60034.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office suite (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook).
  • Willingness to travel and work flexibly in line with project and business requirements.
  • Legal authorisation to work in the United Kingdom (visa sponsorship availability will be assessed based on business and legal requirements).

Preferred

  • Sole British Nationality and current or previous Security Check (SC) clearance (certain project activities may require this — see note below).
  • Experience with product lifecycle management (PLM) or enterprise resource planning (ERP) software such as Teamcenter or SAP.
  • Experience in scheduling, planning, and programme management in an engineering environment.
  • Strong influencing and negotiation skills with a track record of delivering results in cross-functional team environments.

🔒 Security Clearance Note: Some aspects of this role may involve access to information or facilities requiring UK government Security Check (SC) clearance. Candidates who hold or have previously held SC clearance, or who are eligible to obtain it, are encouraged to apply. SC clearance requires sole British Nationality. If you are unsure whether this applies to your situation, please speak with the recruiter.

Why GE Vernova

GE Vernova is a global energy technology company on a mission to electrify and decarbonise the world. Our Rugby site is a centre of expertise in power conversion and rotating machine technology — working on programmes that directly support the energy transition at scale. You'll join a team of specialists who combine deep technical knowledge with a genuine drive to innovate, and you'll have the space to lead, learn, and grow.

At ENGIE, we accelerate the energy transition by harnessing renewable energy sources that make a real difference. Our anaerobic digestion facilities turn organic waste into clean energy, and we need skilled people to keep them running at peak performance.

 

We are looking for a hands-on Maintenance Engineer to join our team at Gorst Energy AD Plant. You will play a vital role in keeping critical infrastructure operational, reducing downtime, and driving continuous improvement. If you thrive in a practical, fast-paced environment and want your work to contribute to a sustainable future, this role is for you.

 

Summary of what you will do

 

  • Carry out preventative and reactive mechanical maintenance to maximise plant uptime and operational efficiency.
  • Diagnose complex technical and mechanical faults on critical plant assets, performing root cause analysis and producing corrective action reports.
  • Develop and implement proactive maintenance procedures and strategies alongside the Maintenance Manager to reduce unplanned failures.
  • Monitor IT control systems, respond to alarms, and produce operational reports, including remote monitoring during on-call periods.
  • Manage permits to work, oversee third-party contractors on site, and ensure full compliance with health and safety policies and procedures.
  • Support plant operations including feedstock loading, weighbridge duties, daily checks, and site housekeeping to maintain a safe and organised environment.
  • Coordinate spare parts stock control, supplier relationships, and purchase order processes to eliminate downtime caused by lack of materials.

 

What you will bring to the role

 

  • A relevant qualification in Mechanical or Electrical Engineering (apprenticeship, City and Guilds, NVQ, HNC, HND, or equivalent proven experience).
  • Solid experience in mechanical maintenance within an industrial or operational plant environment.
  • Good knowledge of anaerobic digestion or similar process-driven systems.
  • IOSH Managing Safely certification and strong understanding of health and safety management, including risk assessments and safe systems of work.
  • First Aid/Fire Warden holder
  • Telehandler licence and experience operating plant machinery.
  • Additional certifications such as confined space, PASMA, or IPAF are desirable.
  • Excellent diagnostic, analytical, and IT skills with the ability to interpret data and solve process issues.
  • A proactive, hands-on attitude with strong communication skills, resilience, and the ability to work independently and as part of a team.
  • Full UK driving licence

 

Location

 

Gorst Energy AD Plant – On Site. This role includes weekend working as part of a team rota. Ideally you will be located within 30 minutes of the plant. A full UK driving licence is essential.

 

What We Offer

 

  • A competitive salary with clear career progression pathways within ENGIE's growing renewable energy portfolio.
  • A diverse range of missions combining mechanical maintenance, process optimisation, and operational support — no two days are the same.
  • Stimulating, meaningful work that directly contributes to the UK's clean energy goals.
  • A friendly, collaborative team environment where knowledge sharing and mutual support are valued.
  • Training and development opportunities including specialist certifications and safety qualifications.
  • Flexibility within the rota structure, supporting work-life balance alongside operational needs.

 

Our Commitment

 

At ENGIE, every talent has a role to play in accelerating the energy transition. Make a difference and enjoy a fulfilling professional experience. Take on exciting challenges and build a career path that reflects who you are. Join us and be part of the adventure of the century!

Your role

As the Manufacturing Engineering Manager - Development, you will play a pivotal role within the Product Development organisation by spearheading the advancement of manufacturing engineering capabilities. Your primary mission is to ensure that our new products are optimized for manufacture, assembly, testing, quality, cost efficiency, and ongoing serviceability from the earliest stages of concept through to full industrialisation. Reporting directly to the Engineering Manager, you will be entrusted with leading a highly skilled Manufacturing Engineering (ME) team, cultivating a culture that values inclusivity, continuous improvement, and technical excellence.

Your leadership responsibilities include mentoring, coaching, and developing your team through clear communication, constructive feedback, and fostering a supportive environment that encourages professional growth and collaboration. You will champion design for excellence (DFx) strategies across various dimensions including Design for Manufacture (DFM), Design for Assembly (DFA), Design for Test (DFT), Design for Service (DFS), and cost-based design to embed robust manufacturability and scalability into our product suites.

You will establish and enforce rigorous standards for Process Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (PFMEA) and Design Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (DFMEA), ensuring early identification and mitigation of risks. Your expertise will guide manufacturing considerations during concept selection, architecture definition, and throughout detailed design reviews, embedding manufacturing requirements from the outset. Additionally, you will define and maintain standardized New Product Introduction (NPI) deliverables, encompassing manufacturability assessments, process assumptions, build standards, routings, and industrialisation readiness criteria.

In this role, you will ensure active and effective participation of your team in technical reviews, manufacturing reviews, and the production control processes to help deliver right-first-time product launches. As the technical authority, you will provide deep knowledge of electronics and electromechanical manufacturing processes, including printed circuit assembly (PCA), box build, testing, and system integration, ensuring design compatibility with current and emerging manufacturing technologies aligned with global production strategies.

This engineering operations technician position serves as the on-site maintenance technician and operator for an AWS data centre.
The Data Centre Engineering Operations Technician (EOT) is responsible for operating and maintaining all electrical, mechanical, emergency generator, and fire/life safety equipment within the data centre. The EOT serves as a technical resource to support Amazon within its data centres. Data centre equipment that supports mission-critical servers must maintain better than 99.999% uptime. jobTitle: Senior Data Center Engineer, Mechanical Engineering
jobDescription:
Remote location: United Kingdom.

Minimum qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree in Mechanical or Industrial Engineering, a related discipline, or equivalent practical experience.
  • 5 years of experience in mission critical facility design and construction environments.
  • Experience in mechanical infrastructure.

Preferred qualifications:

  • Master's degree in Engineering, Business, or other relevant fields, or a Professional Engineering (PE) license.
  • Experience in estimating, mechanical design, operation, and commissioning of mission critical data center mechanical equipment.
  • Experience in design, construction, and commissioning of mechanical cooling plants, fire suppression systems, fuel oil systems, domestic water systems, and sanitary sewer systems.
  • Experience in designing complex modular building scale assemblies, with an understanding of mechanical tolerances and tolerance analysis.
  • Knowledge of mechanical engineering and design principles in the areas of design for medium-scale production, structural beams/elements, and international building codes.
  • Operational knowledge of construction safety procedures.

About the job

Our thirst for technology is a part of everything we do. The Data Center Engineering team takes the physical design of our data centers into the future. Our lab mirrors a research and development department -- cutting-edge strategies are born, tested and tested again. Along with a team of great minds, you take on complex topics like how we use power or how to run state-of-the-art, environmentally-friendly facilities. You're a visionary who optimizes for efficiencies and never stops seeking improvements -- even small changes that can make a huge impact. You generate ideas, communicate recommendations to senior-level executives and drive implementation alongside facilities technicians.

With your technical expertise, you ensure compliance with codes and standards, develop infrastructure improvements and serve as an expert in your specialty (e.g., cooling, electrical).

As a Senior Data Center Engineer, you will be an integral member of the Data Center Delivery and Engineering (DCDE) team which is a collection of Civils Structure, Architecture (CSA), and Mechanical, Electrical, Plumbing (MEP) design experts, mechanical and electrical field engineers, construction project managers, water/air experts, commissioning experts, data center services managers, and cost and project controls managers who design, schedule, construct, commission and close out the most efficient data centers in the world, at a fast-pace, safely and in a scalable manner.

Behind everything our users see online is the architecture built by the Technical Infrastructure team to keep it running. From developing and maintaining our data centers to building the next generation of Google platforms, we make Google's product portfolio possible. We're proud to be our engineers' engineers and love voiding warranties by taking things apart so we can rebuild them. We keep our networks up and running, ensuring our users have the best and fastest experience possible.

Responsibilities

  • Define data center system-level, product architecture, and research and development, while helping to develop operations and maintenance procedures for systems/processes.
  • Conduct engineering analysis and research designs and methods of data center equipment and facilities.
  • Ensure designs and installations meet requirements (e.g., predicted cooling, structural, operational concerns, etc.).
  • Provide technical leadership to the projects, support and optimize project design, scope, schedule, quality, commissioning, and safety for the Mechanical discipline, and provide feedback to the central partner teams on possible improvements.
  • Provide mechanical technical leadership, resolving critical field issues.

Mechanical Building Services Engineer

The successful candidate will be responsible for delivering planned preventative maintenance (PPM), reactive maintenance, fault finding, and repairs across a range of mechanical building services systems. The role requires a strong understanding of commercial building services, with a focus on maintaining safe, efficient, and compliant operations within a customer-facing environment.

Key Responsibilities
  • Carry out planned preventative maintenance (PPM) on mechanical building services plant and equipment in accordance with maintenance schedules and statutory requirements.
  • Undertake reactive maintenance and fault-finding activities on building services systems, ensuring minimal disruption to operations.
  • Maintain and repair mechanical systems including HVAC equipment, pumps, pipework, water services, heating systems, pressurisation units, expansion vessels, and associated plant.

  • Recognised mechanical or plumbing apprenticeship, NVQ Level 3, City & Guilds, or equivalent qualification in Mechanical Engineering, Plumbing, or Building Services.

  • Good understanding of HVAC systems, heating systems, water services, pumps, and associated mechanical plant.
  • Knowledge of health and safety legislation and safe systems of work.
  • Experience using CAFM systems such as Maximo, Concept, or similar.
  • Ability to work independently and as part of a team.
  • Strong communication and customer service skills.
Desirable
  • Water Hygiene awareness or L8 experience.
  • BMS monitoring experience.
  • F-Gas qualification.
  • Experience within corporate offices, commercial properties, or critical environments.
  • First Aid, IPAF, or PASMA certification.

About Linxon

Linxon is a joint venture between Hitachi Energy and SNC-Lavalin, specializing in the engineering, procurement, and construction (EPC) delivery of electrical substations and grid infrastructure projects worldwide. At Hinkley Point C, Linxon is responsible for the delivery of critical high-voltage electrical infrastructure supporting the UK's newest nuclear power station.

 

Position Overview

The Construction Manager will lead all site construction activities associated with the delivery of Linxon's electrical balance-of-plant infrastructure at Hinkley Point C. The role is responsible for ensuring safe, efficient, and compliant execution of construction works, including civil, structural, mechanical, and electrical installation activities.

 

The successful candidate will provide leadership to multidisciplinary construction teams and contractors while maintaining alignment with nuclear safety standards, project schedule commitments, quality requirements, and budget objectives.

 

Key Responsibilities

Construction Leadership

  • Lead all onsite construction activities.
  • Drive a strong safety-first culture aligned with HPC and Linxon requirements.
  • Ensure construction works are delivered in accordance with project specifications, programme, quality requirements, and approved methodologies.
  • Coordinate daily site operations across multiple contractors and interfaces.
  • Provide visible leadership and direction to construction supervisors and contractor management teams.


Health, Safety, Environment and Security

  • Promote and uphold the highest standards of health, safety, environmental, and nuclear safety performance.
  • Ensure compliance with CDM Regulations, HPC site rules, permit-to-work systems, and Linxon HSE procedures.
  • Lead construction safety reviews, inspections, audits, and toolbox talks.
  • Investigate incidents and implement corrective and preventive actions.
  • Support achievement of Zero Harm objectives.


Project Planning and Delivery

  • Develop and implement construction execution strategies.
  • Monitor progress against baseline schedules and identify recovery actions where necessary.
  • Coordinate resource planning, logistics, material deliveries, and site access requirements.
  • Participate in schedule reviews and construction readiness assessments.
  • Manage construction risks, constraints, and interface issues.


Contractor Management

  • Manage principal contractors, subcontractors, and specialist installation teams.
  • Monitor contractor performance against safety, quality, productivity, and schedule metrics.
  • Review contractor work packs, RAMS, lift plans, and construction methodologies.
  • Facilitate coordination meetings and drive resolution of construction challenges.
  • Ensure adequate supervision and competency management across all work fronts.


Quality Assurance

  • Ensure all construction works are executed in accordance with approved drawings, specifications, ITPs, and quality standards.
  • Support inspection and test activities.
  • Manage punch list closure and handover documentation.
  • Ensure non-conformances are identified, recorded, and resolved effectively.
  • Promote a right-first-time approach to construction execution.


Interface and Stakeholder Management

  • Liaise with HPC delivery teams, EDF stakeholders, designers, commissioning teams, and regulatory representatives.
  • Coordinate interfaces between civil, mechanical, electrical, and commissioning activities.
  • Support project reporting and provide regular updates on construction performance.
  • Represent Linxon in client and stakeholder meetings as required.

 

Commercial and Performance Management

  • Support cost management and forecasting activities.
  • Monitor productivity and resource utilization.
  • Identify change opportunities and constructability improvements.
  • Contribute to project KPI reporting and performance reviews.

 


Qualifications

Essential

  • Degree or HNC/HND in Construction Management, Electrical Engineering, Civil Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or related discipline.
  • SMSTS Certification.
  • Strong understanding of Construction Design & Management (CDM) Regulations.
  • Full UK Driving Licence.


Desirable

  • Membership of CIOB, ICE, IET, APM, or equivalent professional body.
  • Nuclear industry qualifications and training.
  • Temporary Works Coordinator certification.
  • NEBOSH Construction Certificate.

 

Experience

Essential

  • Significant experience managing large-scale industrial, infrastructure, power, utility, or energy construction projects.
  • Proven experience delivering HV electrical infrastructure, substations, grid connections, or EPC projects.
  • Experience managing multiple contractors in a highly regulated environment.
  • Demonstrated leadership in achieving high safety performance standards.
  • Experience managing complex construction interfaces and stakeholder relationships.


Desirable

  • Previous nuclear industry experience.
  • Experience working on Hinkley Point C or major UK infrastructure projects.
  • Knowledge of ONR and nuclear quality requirements.

 

What We Offer

  • Opportunity to work on one of Europe's largest and most complex infrastructure projects.
  • Career development within a global EPC organisation.
  • Collaborative and safety-focused working environment.
  • Competitive salary, bonus, pension, and benefits package.

About us: 

You will join the Laboratory Test Means development team. We are responsible for the development, modification and maintenance of test rigs for Fuel and Landing Gear Systems. Our skill sets include electrical design, fluid mechanical and mechanical design and test facility operations. We are not your typical office based environment as we work directly with equipment often in hazardous environments involving Jet Fuel, Hydraulic Fluid, Hot and Cold surfaces, Noise and High voltages.

Our role is to develop the means for Airbus to test new technologies and system evolutions for the Landing Gear and Fuel systems of todays aircraft and tomorrows. Life in the test centre is dynamic and day to day you can find yourself working on different topics; from supporting setting up a test for an in-service aircraft issue to understanding how to integrate a new technology into a test rig.

What you will be doing:

  • End to end development of new test rigs; from requirements capture to detailed design to manufacturing/integration and commissioning of the test rig;

  • Supporting the modification of existing test rigs to support a new test request;

  • Troubleshooting test rig issues;

  • Utilising CATIA and other tooling to produce 3D digital mock-ups, bill of materials and build procedures;

  • Working within a non-office based environment with access to prototyping areas, avionic and fluid mechanical test rigs.

companyLocation: Didcot or Swindon or Little Barford
jobLocation: Didcot or Swindon or Little Barford
jobDescription:
Mechanical Engineering Placement Programme - Rotating Equipment

Location(s): 

Didcot, OXF, GB, OX11 7YU Swindon, Wiltshire, GB, SN5 6PB Little Barford, CAM, GB, PE19 6YT

RWE Generation UK
Start date on 28th June 2027, full time, fixed term (13 months)

Are you interested in a placement with one of the UK’s largest energy producers? Our Rotating Equipment Team has an exciting industrial placement opportunity, and is looking for a motivated team member with excellent interpersonal skills.

 

RWE Generation’s Engineering and Outage (E&O) group supports our portfolio of gas-fired power stations across Europe. The Rotating Equipment team is responsible for the technical engineering strategy, performance and risk management for gas turbines and steam turbines within the RWE gas division portfolio. A placement with the Rotating Equipment team will allow you to work within this dynamic and international group of engineers, and will be based either at RWE’s UK head office in Swindon or at one of RWE’s UK power station sites. You will also have opportunities to support the rest of the fleet remotely, and will have benefit from being able to visit and work at sites other than your base location.

 

About the role

  • Work alongside Mechanical Engineers to resolve real engineering problems that directly affect the portfolio.
  • Undertake data analysis to diagnose problems to help in both long and short term projects.
  • Gain important on-site experience and valuable hands-on practical skills.
  • Enjoy using your problem solving and teamworking skills to successfully deliver your responsibilities.
  • Attend courses, workshops and on the job training for your personal development.

 

You may also have the opportunity to spend time with other disciplines, such as shift work with our operations section, taking on the day-to-day challenges that come with operating a power station.

 

Job requirements and experience

  • Ideally, you should be studying a BEng or MEng Mechanical Engineering degree at an undergraduate level.
  • A valid driving licence is preferred, as the placement may involve travel to different RWE sites.

 

If your degree is in a similar Engineering, Maths or Science discipline and you have an interest in the energy industry, we’d love to hear from you!

 

Your benefits

  • An attractive salary.
  • A personal retirement savings plan – if you put in 5% we will top up by a further 10% and you will get life assurance worth 4 x annual salary.
  • 25 days annual leave plus bank holidays, pro-rata.
  • Access to flexible benefits such as Critical Illness, Dental Plan, Health Cash Plan, Share Incentive Plan, Cycle2Work, Electric Car Lease Scheme, Buy Additional Annual Leave and retail savings scheme.
  • Occupational Health support services for your wellbeing.
  • Access to our employee assistance programme in times of need.
  • Up to 2 days volunteering a year.

 

To view a preview of our benefits site ‘YourHub’ and see some of the other benefits we have on offer please visit YourHub.

Any questions? Contact HR: Lisa Merryweather, +44 786 7370980

We look forward to meeting you. Of course, you can find us on LinkedIn, Instagram, Facebook, YouTube and Xing, too.


We value diversity and therefore welcome all applications - regardless of gender, disability, nationality, ethnic and social origin, religion/belief, age, sexual orientation, and identity. #inclusionmatters


RWE Generation provides a flexible mix for a powerful future. With a team of around 3,500 employees, the company operates flexible gas power plants, bioenergy facilities, and hydropower stations in Germany, the Netherlands, the UK, and Turkey. These assets play a vital role in balancing the supply of renewable energy during periods of fluctuation, thereby ensuring the stability of the power grid. Recognising the importance of energy storage, RWE Generation is integrating battery systems into its operations and pioneering hydrogen-powered technologies - an essential element for storing renewable energy for when it is needed most. As a long-standing partner for the regions in which we operate, our reliable, clean and flexible assets enable us to play a key role in decarbonising the energy system. Our team continues to be inventive, using their experience, talent and sunrise technologies to be the cornerstone our society can rely on.
